popov.title: Discrete complex reflection groups
exact_supported_facts: Popov numbering agrees with Shephard-Todd numbering
No. 12 is GL(2,3), dimension 2, over the ring Z[i*sqrt(2)]
Table 2 gives [K12] with translation lattice [1,i*sqrt(2)]e1 + [1,i*sqrt(2)]e2 and cocycle c=0
Table 2 gives [K12]* with c(r1)=c(r2)=0 and c(r3)=((1+i)/2)e3
for fixed linear group K and translation lattice T, an affine extension defines a class in H^1(K,V/T)
changing the chosen base point changes the cocycle by a 1-coboundary
the crystallographic reflection-group extension classes form a subgroup of H^1(K,V/T) of order at most 2
[K12]* is one of the non-semidirect crystallographic reflection groups

krr.title: The Bolza curve and some orbifold ball quotient surfaces
exact_supported_facts: up to conjugation there are two GL2(F3) actions on A: the affine G48 action with no global fixed point and its linear part with translations forgotten, fixing 0
the Abel-Jacobi embedding alpha sends infinity to 0 before the later conjugating automorphism is applied
the curve-preserving affine action has translation term [g(infinity)]-[infinity]
there exists an automorphism g of A with H48=g G48 g^-1
the checked source changes the embedding by composing with this g before identifying H48 and G48, but does not materialize g pointwise on the six Weierstrass points

semantic_boundary.reason: Popov resolves the affine extension class up to the cohomological/conjugacy equivalence used in its classification. KRR supplies existence of a conjugating automorphism between the curve-preserving affine action and Deraux G48, but the checked sources do not bind Popov's cocycle basis/generators or KRR infinity/zero to one retained Deraux six-point coordinate. Thus no pointwise source-to-target marking is obtained.
